Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

this is a big issue with the "bash for everything" approach

if you look you'll see it using python for edits then && run tests && format for every single change

it's too loose https://t.co/GGYb9jpcEh

i see people saying

they're moving to iac because agents
they're not using iac because agents
they're switching to a monorepos because agents
they're moving off monorepos because agents

you're all confused man everyone is doing random shit

our github triage system works off a long running opencode session

this means it will delegate work to subagents that have previously worked on something similar

so specialized subagents will naturally emerge - here we have a linux fuckery subagent https://t.co/F1hlNgl4Wt

こないだのLinuxカーネル（TCPのUAF）の件とは違って「全員関係ある」わけではないけど、対象のインフラを組んでいる人にとっては背筋が凍るCVSS 10.0（満点）の脆弱性が出た。  UbuntuのCanonical社が開発するコンテナ・仮想マシン基盤「LXD」の脆弱性（CVE-2026-112816）。
これうち大丈夫みたい。
Brotli のデコーダ脆弱性（CVE-2026-111497）が CISA の悪用確認済み脆弱性カタログ（KEV）に追加。細工した圧縮データでメモリ破壊や任意コード実行の可能性。Node.js は node:zlib で信頼できない Brotli を展開する場合が対象、修正版は 26.12.1 / 24.22.1 / 22.23.4 🤖自動投稿
Linuxカーネルの脆弱性CVE-2026-98432（CVSS 9.8）。IPv4のTCP受付処理のメモリ解放ミスで、ログイン不要の遠隔攻撃のおそれ。Debianは修正済、Ubuntu・RHELは準備中。修正が出たらカーネル更新＋再起動を。当面はRed Hatの緩和策も。#脆弱性 #Linux https://t.co/tNN6pfOrmR

Claude Code 2.1.314 adds permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories: Write/Edit refuse paths outside the working directory in every permission mode. A cheap, enforceable guardrail for teams rolling out coding agents.

Claude Code on the web keeps GitHub credentials behind a proxy that checks which branch a push targets. For coding agents, keeping secrets outside the sandbox is only part of the design: constrain what the credential can authorize, too.

Installing random agent skills off GitHub? NVIDIA has an open-source scanner for that.

SkillSpector checks Claude Code, Codex and MCP skills before you run them:

• 71 patterns in 17 categories: prompt injection, data exfiltration, privilege escalation, supply chain, memory poisoning
• Fast static pass + optional LLM review
• 0-100 risk score, output as terminal, JSON, Markdown or SARIF
• Scans a repo, URL, zip, folder or single SKILL.md

Their research subset: 26.1% of 31k skills had vulnerabilities, 5.2% looked malicious.

~23.8k stars, Apache-2.0.

https://t.co/XM4UkhMme8
